selection.reason: Both candidate point estimates improve over IR305 and IR306; IR306 comparisons exclude zero in both cohorts. The first IR305 interval and both same-runtime-ablation intervals cross zero. Retain the native lowering and instruction reduction for further work, but keep IR305 as the conservative established speed reference. No latency rerun of this unchanged candidate.

fastest_processing_Rust.scope: Fastest explicitly documented post-JSON timer including input preparation and worker creation/run/join. Artifact restoration and JSON IO are tracked in whole-process time.

fastest_whole_Rust.scope: Fastest external fresh process, launch through exit, including all setup, JSON IO, computation and teardown.

limitations: Counters include diagnostic probes and tracked-allocator observation; coarse and detailed instrumentation must be compared separately.
Mech phase0 includes canonical input admission, session setup and immutable-snapshot work absent in Rust. Necessary work differs, despite aligned semantic boundaries.
No worker elapsed-time sums are used; coarse elapsed time and process counters are continuous main-thread boundary snapshots.

Query phase includes worker create/run/join, index/other internal cleanup, result export/materialization. Rust generate temporary destruction is included even though its old inner query timer excluded part of it.

Detailed callback subscopes are inclusive; outside_binding_and_invocation is a disjoint residual containing wrapper preparation, binding destruction, probes and publication work outside invoke_scoped.
